Problem: Need for adaptive retrieval in hybrid text-graph RAG; existing systems rely on fixed pipelines, lacking ability to integrate supplementary evidence as reasoning unfolds; graph evidence expensive.

Method: RouteRAG, RL-based framework that jointly optimizes entire generation process via RL, learns when to reason, what to retrieve from texts or graphs, and when to produce final answers; two-stage training framework accounting for task outcome and retrieval efficiency.

Key assumptions: RL can effectively learn retrieval policy; efficiency reward encourages minimal retrieval turns; hybrid retrieval complementary.

Main contribution: RouteRAG enables adaptive multi-turn graph-text hybrid RAG via RL, outperforming baselines on five QA benchmarks.

Datasets: PopQA, Natural Questions, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue.

Baselines: existing graph-based and multi-turn RAG systems (e.g., HippoRAG 2, etc.)

Metrics: Exact Match (EM) and F1 scores.

Results: RouteRAG significantly outperforms existing RAG baselines; e.g., RouteRAG-7B achieves EM scores: PopQA 50.6, NQ 56.4, HotpotQA 51.5, 2Wiki 60.4, MuSiQue 60.8 (with ∗ indicating in-domain). Actually the table shows numbers; we can summarize.

Limitations: RL training only on 3B and 7B LLMs due to compute; uses HippoRAG 2 as graph retriever; may not generalize to larger models.

Future work: not stated.

Code availability: publicly available at https://github.com/YucanGuo/RouteRAG.

Method: KG-Reasoner, an end-to-end framework that integrates multi-step reasoning into a unified "thinking" phase of a Reasoning LLM; uses RL to train LLM to internalize KG traversal, enabling dynamic path exploration and backtracking.

Key assumptions: RL can effectively train LLM to internalize KG traversal; end-to-end reasoning preserves critical intermediate information; retrieval tool provides triples for reasoning.

Main contribution: KG-Reasoner achieves competitive or superior performance on eight multi-hop and knowledge-intensive reasoning benchmarks compared to state-of-the-art methods; code available.

Datasets: eight datasets: four Freebase-based (CWQ, WebQuestionsSP, WebQuestions, GrailQA) and four WikiData-based (QALD10-en, T-REx, Zero-Shot RE, Creak).

Limitations: Improving reasoning capability during "think" stage often requires RL, which incurs computational overhead (GRPO); method does not directly address KG incompleteness and noise.
